agentreins-moblie uses apps on a separate virtual screen so you can keep using your phone. That needs Android 13 or later; this phone runs Android %1$s, so tasks can’t start yet.

agentreins-moblie uses the accessibility service to read and control its own virtual screen. Find agentreins-moblie under Accessibility in system settings (on some phones it’s under “Downloaded apps” or “Installed services”) and turn it on.

System settings show agentreins-moblie’s accessibility service as on, but it isn’t actually running (this often happens after agentreins-moblie is force-stopped). Turn agentreins-moblie off in accessibility settings, then on again.
agentreins-moblie needs a large language model with tool calling to think and act. Just enter the provider’s URL, the model name and an API key.

On Android 13, background work may affect focus on your screen: when agentreins-moblie opens an app or scrolls on the virtual screen, the field you’re typing in may briefly lose focus and need another tap. From Android 14 the virtual screen has its own focus. This phone runs Android %1$s; tasks still work normally.
Once allowed, task progress and “Needs you” alerts show in the shade and on the lock screen. agentreins-moblie works without them, you just won’t see these alerts.
